thread:
maria: heads-up — proposal to collapse route_quota + route_meta into a single partitioned table (route_profile) for faster dashboard joins. currently console does a 3-way join on route, quota, tags which is killing p99 on big orgs.

aditya: curious — how big is 'big'? any perf numbers?

maria: on a 10k-route tenant we see dashboard query p99 ~1.2s and CPU spikes during audit scans. single-join expected to drop p99 to ~200–300ms in local tests.

sam: what's the migration plan? backfill + dual-write? any locks?

maria: plan draft:
1) create route_profile (partitioned by tenant_id, route_id as clustering key)
2) dualwrite from API (v2 quota writes go to route_profile) behind a feature flag
3) backfill in small batches using per-tenant cursor, with throttling and checksum validation
4) switch console reads to route_profile via a read-rollout (canary tenants)

jess: +1 for dual-write. needs idempotency keys and a reconciliation job. also we should expose a migration-status endpoint for the console UX to show readiness per-tenant.

patrick: important: avoid large table rewrites that bloat WAL. do incremental INSERT ... ON CONFLICT updates, and set low maintenance_work_mem for backfill windows. maybe use COPY for brand-new partitions.

infra-bot: deployment note — enabling dual-write flag will create 2x writes per request; watch for RPS on ingest-proxy.

aditya: how will alerts change? current quota-alerting reads quota table; changing reads to route_profile could break historical dashboards unless we keep a shadow view.

maria: yeah we plan to keep a read-only view quota_view that unions legacy tables until we sunset them. Also will add a migration column `source_version` so we can trace rows created by backfill vs live writes.

eli: console query layer needs a new index for 'last_seen_token_ts' — dashboards filter on recent activity. propose a covering index on (tenant_id, last_seen_token_ts DESC) INCLUDE (quota_limit, route_status).

sam: UX/rollout ask: expose per-tenant migration progress in console -> settings -> infra so support can see ETA and pause backfills for problematic tenants.

maria: agreed. action items:
- aditya: spec the migration-status endpoint and schema for progress (ETA, rows_processed, error_count) — due EOD Tue
- patrick: backfill playbook with throttling knobs and WAL/maintenance guidance — due Wed
- jess: add idempotency + reconciliation skeleton to repo (shallow PR) — due Thu
- infra: monitor proxy RPS during dual-write canary (infra-bot will post)

maria: also open question — we should consider materialized views for common dashboard panels to avoid repeated heavy joins. cheap to maintain with incremental refresh? thoughts?

aditya: materialized view for the 7-day active routes panel seems promising. we can refresh per-tenant on a schedule or on write with a small event. avoid global refresh.

maria: sweet. I'll move the spec to the doc page and start a short RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:

jess: fyi I'll add a lightweight schema migration test that runs a sample backfill on a snapshot DB (sanitized) to validate checksum and runtime estimates.

infra-bot: alert — canary dual-write enabled for tenant id 9001 at 2951112600

aditya: saw metrics — write p95 latency +3ms, stages look healthy. will post detailed numbers tomorrow.

maria: closing loop — tagging @support for awareness and I'll post the RFC link in #eng-platform when ready.
